subject: Private deploy: proposal for 'witnessless' snapshot exhibit & Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Connors <sara.connors@carenix.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 27 Jun 2028 16:32:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy: proposal for 'witnessless' snapshot exhibit & Order Form redlines

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the detailed run-through on the call today. Attached is a short proposal for responding to Carenix's request for an "operator evidence" exhibit while keeping the deployment practical for our engineering/ops teams. The high-level idea is an optional "witnessless snapshot" pathway that avoids a live witness requirement but preserves auditability. Key bullets: 

- What we propose: Redwood will provide a signed, timestamped snapshot of the runtime image and a manifest (checksums + build metadata). No third-party physical witness required.
- Limited forensic access: Carenix can request an on-site or remote forensic access session within a 30-day audit window; access uses a scoped read-only console token and a temporary VPN session.
- License scope: snapshot + runtime image permitted for recovery and verification only; Carenix cannot use the snapshot to spin up independent production endpoints without a conversion license and operations review.
- Escrow alternative: if Carenix insists on traditional escrow/witnessing, we can support that via a mutually-agreed vendor (costs and schedule TBD).
- Operational guardrails: ephemeral operator tokens, rolling proofs, and canary execute test that Redwood will perform to verify snapshot bootability prior to handover.

Attached: OrderForm_Exhibit-Snapshot-Proposal.pdf (proposal language), Carenix_MSA_Redline_v1.docx (our current redlines), ops-runbook-outline.md (ops-level notes).

Ask: Please review the exhibit language and let us know whether (1) this meets Carenix's risk needs or (2) we should prepare for a witnessed-escrow path. If you prefer the witnessless path, we need legal redline suggestions on 4 clauses: license scope, audit window and scope, indemnity & limitation carveouts, and rollback/transfer controls.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Sara Connors <sara.connors@carenix.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Carenix Legal <legal@carenix.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 27 Jun 2028 19:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy: proposal for 'witnessless' snapshot exhibit & Order Form redlines

Karthik —

Appreciate the quick write-up and the attachments. A few high-level concerns from our side and our external counsel: 

1) License scope needs clearer prohibitions on spinning up derivative environments. The phrase "for recovery and verification only" is ok but we need a paragraph that defines permitted verification activities and expressly prohibits non-production redeployments.
2) Audit window: 30 days may be tight for our compliance team; can we do 60 days with one renewal option upon reasonable cause (e.g., new regulatory inquiry)? Also we need explicit handling of logs and retention during that window.
3) Forensic access: remote read-only tokens are acceptable only if session recordings and Redmond audit logs are provided to us within 48 hours of the session.
4) Indemnity / liability: our counsel asks that we see Redwood's standard indemnity language if we're foregoing a third-party witness. We expect stronger contractual assurances.

Practically, we like the idea of a non-witness path if Redwood is willing to accept (a) expanded audit window (60d), (b) specified session recordings + log export, and (c) a narrow, enumerated conversion license fee if Carenix later needs to operationalize the snapshot.

I'll circulate this to our GC and recommend we schedule a legal redline call next week. Can you confirm whether Redwood has precedent language for the conversion license fee and whether your compliance team can commit to the session recordings + log export SLA?

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Connors
Head of Procurement, Carenix
sara.connors@carenix.com

Quoted: On Wed, 27 Jun 2028 at 16:32, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> [original proposal attached]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 07:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy: proposal for 'witnessless' snapshot exhibit & Order Form redlines

Karthik / David —

Thanks Sara — good feedback. A quick internal summary and suggested approach for legal: 

- License carve: tighten the exhibit to include a short definition section: "Verification Activities" = checksum validation, boot verification, functional smoke tests in a single non-production namespace; explicitly state these activities do not include scaling, production traffic, or integration with external systems.
- Audit window: offer 60 days as requested but require a single 30-day extension only with a signed request and justification; Redwood must preserve session recordings for 90 days post-session for our own forensics.
- Session logs/recording: we can provide session recordings and sanitized logs. We will require Carenix to sign a narrow NDA addendum for log export and agree to limited use of logs for compliance purposes only.
- Indemnity: legal will not accept open-ended assumptions. Proposed compromise: limited indemnity tied to Redwood's operational negligence during evidence delivery; for any broader liability, escalate to pricing (conversion license + increased support SLA).

Action items for Legal (David): 
1) Draft option A language for the witnessless exhibit (tight definitions + log NDA + conversion license clause).
2) Draft option B fallback language for a witnessed escrow (vendor, cost estimate placeholder) in case Carenix insists.
3) Provide a redline back to Sara by EOD Monday so we can keep the procurement timeline intact.

If David is ok, I'll propose a joint legal call with Carenix on Monday (11am PT) to run through redlines. Thoughts?

Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy: proposal for 'witnessless' snapshot exhibit & Order Form redlines

Sara —

Really appreciate the clear asks; all reasonable. Quick responses: 

- Conversion license: we do have precedent; typical approach is a one-time conversion fee (tiered by model size and support band). I'll include a precedent clause and a placeholder fee table in the next redline.
- Session recordings + logs: compliance can commit to producing session recordings and a structured log export within 48 hours; we will add the NDA-addendum language to govern log handling and retention (Redwood keeps a copy for 90 days for audit purposes).
- Audit window: happy to accept 60 days with one documented 30-day extension if justified.
- Indemnity: agree to a limited indemnity for operator negligence during evidence delivery; broader liability will remain capped per standard MSA limits unless buyer purchases conversion license + elevated SLA.

Next steps: David — can you produce draft A (witnessless exhibit) + draft B (witnessed escrow fallback) and a short comment matrix by EOD Monday (2028-07-01)? I'll schedule the joint redline call for Monday 11am PT and add Sara, her GC, and our legal ops.

Sara — attaching the current precedent clause I referenced and a short FAQ for the conversion license (Conversion_FAQ.pdf). If Monday works, we'll aim to close exhibit language within two negotiation cycles.

Karthik
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
